blocks.text: The magnetic quantum number m describes the orientation of an orbital in space. Within a subshell the value of m depends on l: for a given l there are 2l + 1 integral values of m, from -l through 0 to +l. The values of m give the number of orbitals in a subshell. If l = 0 (an s subshell) the only value is 0, so an s subshell has one orbital. If l = 1 (p) there are three values, -1, 0 and +1, so a p subshell has three orbitals. If l = 2 (d) there are five, -2, -1, 0, +1 and +2, so a d subshell has five orbitals. If l = 3 (f) there are seven, -3 to +3, so an f subshell has seven orbitals. Orbitals of the same subshell have the same energy and are degenerate; they are distinguished from each other in the presence of a magnetic field, hence the name of this quantum number.

blocks.title: Did you know
blocks.text: The splitting of fine spectral lines in the presence of a magnetic field, and their three-dimensional orientation in space, indicate the presence of orbitals in subshells.
